summary: Discovery focused on Mosaic's upcoming campaign spikes and streaming requirements. Main goals: clarify p95 latency targets for streaming short-turn responses, peak concurrency and burst token/sec needs, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and security compliance. Redwood to propose dedicated pool sizing and run pilot benchmarks.
topics: p95 streaming latency targets and measurement
concurrency and sustained tokens/sec vs short burst sizing
hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private control plane
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Chen: thanks everyone for joining, we were told this was the token surge planning, hi priya, ethan, jordan.
[00:06] Priya Patel: yeah thanks, we wanna make sure our chat feature doesn't melt when we push the marketing campaign, so p95 and burst are huge for us.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: cool, quick intro — im marco, se on redwood, i usually run the throughput and streaming profiles.
[00:18] Jordan Kim: quick note — we have hard security constraints, private vpc path preferred but open to dedicated if it meets our residency and k m s needs.
[00:28] Alicia Chen: great. can you walk us through expected traffic shapes? priya?
[00:33] Priya Patel: sure. baseline is ~20 concurrent streams during normal day, each session average 40 tokens in chat, token rate ~8-12 tps per session. campaign worst-case is 400 concurrent users for 10 minutes, and then we see a 10x burst that may go to ~4,000 concurrent for a 5 min window. total token/sec at peak ... ballpark 150k tokens/sec for the campaign spike.
[01:05] Ethan Cole: to add, some flows are streaming — we send partial generations to front-end, so start-of-token latency matters more than final-latency. p95 for initial token is our big metric.
[01:20] Marco Ruiz: understood. what are your p95 targets for short interactions, like 16-64 tokens?
[01:26] Priya Patel: we want p95 initial-token under 200ms for short prompts (<32 tokens) and end-to-end under 900ms for 64-token replies when streamed. If it's too high, UX degrades.
[01:38] Marco Ruiz: that's aggressive but within reason with the right infra. For hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs: Hosted is easiest to start but dedicated gives you predictable tail latency at scale — we usually recommend dedicated pool with autoscale + burst allowance for those predictable campaign spikes.
[01:53] Jordan Kim: how do you price burst? and what about fallback? if dedicated is full, do you route to hosted?
[02:01] Alicia Chen: yes, we can configure smart routing — primary to dedicated, overflow to hosted or a smaller cheaper variant. Pricing for dedicated includes reserve vGPU capacity; burst can be met with short-term pool expansion or fallback to hosted with higher cost. I'll send concrete numbers after we size the pool.
[02:20] Ethan Cole: curious about caching — we have lots of repeated prefixes for the campaign, will that help?
[02:25] Marco Ruiz: absolutely. prefix / KV cache can reduce compute on repeated sequences. in some workloads we see 20-40% token compute reduction. note, kv cache effect depends on prompt variability and model. also quantization options — 8-bit or 4-bit — can lower CPU/GPU utilization but may slightly change quality; we can show eval diffs.
[02:49] Priya Patel: are there any gotchas with streaming and quant? i mean we need stable p95 not just median.
[02:55] Marco Ruiz: good call — quantization sometimes impacts token generation speed per batch and affects kernel selection; on certain GPUs it improves throughput but tail behavior can vary. we'll run both quantized and fp16 passes in the lab to compare p95.
[03:10] Jordan Kim: security side — we must have customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SSO. private control plane is ideal. is that supported?
[03:18] Alicia Chen: yes, Private deployments support VPC, customer KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs. Dedicated can also be VPC-peered and support KMS. we'll include SOC2 docs and the security questionnaire.
[03:29] Priya Patel: timeline — we aim to run a pilot before end of q2, ideally 3 weeks of testing then campaign in late q3. doable?
[03:36] Marco Ruiz: timeline seems tight but doable. for pilot we recommend two phases: 1) focused p95 lab runs with your prompt set and traffic profiles (steady-state + configured surge) 2) 72-hour soak on dedicated pool to observe tail and autoscale behavior.
[03:51] Ethan Cole: how do you actually benchmark streaming p95? we use JMeter currently but it's tricky to simulate token streaming.
[03:59] Marco Ruiz: we give a benchmark harness (python-based) that simulates incremental token reads and measures time-to-first-token and per-token latency. We also instrument KV cache warmup. We can run on your test tokens and share CSV + token-timeline graphs.
[04:15] Priya Patel: what about concurrency testing methodology — we need realistic open connections and pacing to reflect front-end.
[04:20] Marco Ruiz: yes use open connection model with steady arrival and a separate spike scenario. we'll provide a runner that maintains 5 different traffic mixes. also we'll include p95 rolling windows at 1m and 5m to show tail volatility.
[04:34] Jordan Kim: numbers — what pool size would you start with for our baseline vs surge?
[04:38] Marco Ruiz: preliminary guess: for your baseline (20-400 concurrent) probably 4-6 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady (depending on model). to handle 4k concurrent 5-min surge we recommend a burst config that can add another 30-40 GPUs or fallback routing to hosted. exact sizing depends on model LLM size (13B vs 70B), sequence lengths, and if you enable quantization. we'll size precisely after you share prompt set and we run micro-benchmarks.
[05:06] Priya Patel: model — we're planning to use an open 30B variant initially, may move to 70B later. can see differences?
[05:12] Marco Ruiz: yes 30B vs 70B has linear-ish increases in mem and token compute. 70B will increase per-token latency and reduce tokens/sec per GPU; might need 2-3x more GPUs for same p95. that's why caching and quant are important.
[05:25] Ethan Cole: can you give rough tokens/sec per GPU numbers? just to ballpark.
transcript_continued:
[05:30] Marco Ruiz: rough ballpark: on A100-80GB with optimized kernels 30B might be ~120-200 tokens/sec per GPU under streaming-friendly batch sizes; 70B might be ~40-80 tokens/sec. again depends on batch and kernel. with quantization you can often get 1.5-2x throughput.
[05:52] Priya Patel: ok that helps. we need p95 for first token <200ms — is that achievable with 30B at our baseline?
[06:00] Marco Ruiz: yes generally for warm sessions and with small batches it's achievable. cold-starts or missed kv-cache will show higher tails. that's why we recommend prefix cache warmup for campaign windows.
[06:12] Jordan Kim: on fallback — if we route to hosted during overflow, what happens to rate limits and costs?
[06:17] Alicia Chen: hosted has different rate plans; we can set a soft-limit and cost alerts. Overflow to hosted will incur higher per-token cost but keeps UX available. We can also reserve burst credits on dedicated; we'll include costing scenarios in the pricing doc.
[06:33] Ethan Cole: we also have retention concerns — must not persist user messages beyond X days and encryption at rest.
[06:38] Alicia Chen: retention policies can be configured, and Private + Dedicated options give you control over logs; KMS encryption for keys and TLS in transit. we'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[06:50] Priya Patel: what about rollout — can we do canary with a small percent of traffic?
[06:54] Marco Ruiz: yes our rollout supports canary and A/B plus automatic fallback if p95 crosses threshold. you can pin model versions per route.
[07:02] Jordan Kim: perfect. last question — do you support on-prem if required?
[07:06] Alicia Chen: yes we have an on-prem package for regulated workloads; it requires more lead time and an on-site install or air-gapped deliverable; we can run through that in tech deep-dive.
[07:17] Priya Patel: ok next steps recap please.
[07:20] Alicia Chen: recap: marco sends benchmark harness + burst-sizing questionnaire, i share pricing and security docs, set up lab run week of may 10, priya shares prompt set and traffic profiles. pilot target q2 end test window then campaign prep.
[07:34] Ethan Cole: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:37] Jordan Kim: thanks.
[07:39] Alicia Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments. bye.
[07:43] [meeting ended]
